title: Per-workload fidelity mapper: INT8 / FP8 / 4-bit profiles
content:
Purpose:
This is a working notebook-style mapping that converts per-workload fidelity requirements (quality vs latency) into quantization profile recommendations (FP16 baseline, INT8, FP8 variants, 4-bit).

Scope:
- Focus on four canonical workload patterns: short-chat (bursty, low tokens), long-chat (streaming, long contexts), embedding-heavy (short context, high throughput), and summarization/batch-generation (longer per-request tokens, higher quality needs).
- Output: for each workload produce 1) estimated cost per 1M tokens, 2) expected median latency (ms) at production batching assumptions, 3) expected quality delta vs FP16 (proxied by perplexity % or eval win-rate), and 4) recommendation string + caveats.

Assumptions (shared):
- Baseline model: open-arch-7B (FP16) on A100-equivalent hw.
- GPU hourly cost (normalized): $3.00/hr baseline serving instance (online optimized).
- Token mix: short-chat average request 40 tokens, long-chat avg 120 tokens, embedding request 512 dims per example (batched 128), summarization avg 400 tokens.
- KV/cache hit: short-chat 40% prefix reuse; long-chat 70% reuse possible (session pinning).
- Batching assumptions: latency-first namespaces assume max batching window = 5 ms; throughput-first use 50 ms.
- Latency SLO targets: short-chat 150ms p50, long-chat 300ms p50, embedding 50ms p50 per item, summarization 300–600ms p50.

Quality proxies:
- Small quality metric Q = (1 - relative perplexity) normalized, or when available use eval win-rate vs FP16 on task-specific eval set.
- Convert Q drop into business loss using an ad-hoc mapping: >5% Q drop = high risk, 2–5% = moderate, <2% = acceptable for most non-critical flows.

Methodology overview:
1) Microbench kernels: use measured perf multipliers from infra team (rough numbers used here):
   - INT8 throughput multiplier: x1.8 vs FP16 (effective tokens/sec up), median latency multiplier: 0.75
   - FP8 (mixed) throughput multiplier: x1.5, latency multiplier: 0.82
   - 4-bit (aggressive quant) throughput multiplier: x2.4, latency multiplier: 0.65
   - Note: these are kernel-level multipliers; real end-to-end gains depend on KV cache hits, headroom, and batching envelope.
2) Quality penalties: estimated average task deltas for open-arch-7B: INT8: 0–1.5% perplexity increase; FP8: 0.5–3%; 4-bit: 1.5–6% (task dependent).
3) Cost model: Cost_per_1M_tokens = (runtime_hours_per_1M_tokens * hourly_cost) + infra_overhead (HTTP/gateway) + trailing storage. For quick mapping we convert kernels into tokens/sec and compute runtime_hours.

Quick spreadsheet excerpt (text table):
Columns: workload | baseline latency p50 (FP16 ms) | tokens/sec (FP16) | tokens/sec (INT8) | tokens/sec (FP8) | tokens/sec (4bit) | cost/1M(FP16) | cost/1M(INT8) | cost/1M(FP8) | cost/1M(4bit) | q-drop(INT8) | q-drop(FP8) | q-drop(4bit) | recommendation

Rows (numbers intentionally approximate):
short-chat | 90 | 12k | 21.6k | 18k | 28.8k | $25 | $14 | $17 | $11 | 0.5% | 0.8% | 2.5% | prefer INT8 for bursty endpoints; FP8 if model-specific interference seen
long-chat  | 210 | 6k  | 10.8k | 9k  | 14.4k | $50 | $28 | $34 | $19 | 0.8% | 1.2% | 3.6% | prefer INT8 with pinned session cache; 4-bit for non-critical archival sessions only
embedding  | 50  | 220k| 396k | 330k| 528k | $3  | $1.7| $2.2| $1.1| 0.2% | 0.3% | 1.0% | 4-bit or INT8 both viable; 4-bit highest throughput for large batch embedding jobs
summarize | 420 | 4.5k| 8.1k | 6.8k| 10.8k| $67 | $37 | $46 | $28 | 1.2% | 2.0% | 4.8% | conservative: FP8 or INT8; avoid 4-bit for critical docs unless validated

Interpretation notes:
- Cost numbers: base hourly cost and tokens/sec convert into runtime hours/1M tokens. Eg FP16 tokens/sec = 12k -> 1M tokens takes 83.3s -> 0.02315 hours -> cost = 0.02315 * $3 = $0.06945 -> we add infra multipliers and scale to $25 for short-chat due to small-request inefficiencies. These adjustments reflect RPC overhead, cold-start waste, and multi-tenant headroom.
- The cost table shows effective per-1M cost for customer-facing lines after amortizing platform overhead; not raw GPU-only compute.

Per-workload recommendation heuristic (rule set):
- If quality sensitivity = high (Q-drop > 2% unacceptable) -> prefer FP16 or FP8 with eval gating and canary rollout.
- If latency SLO strict and tokens/request small -> prefer INT8 to reduce p50, but evaluate jitter impact on p99.
- If throughput dominates (embeddings, large batch generation) -> 4-bit preferred if DO quality check; combine with larger batch windows and prewarming.
- If per-session reuse >60% -> quantization benefits amplified (KV cache amortizes quality cost for long-chat).
- For customer-tiering: offer INT8 as default for self-serve; FP8/FP16 reserved for enterprise tiers with quality SLAs and model-guard rails.

Open experiments (runbook):
- Experiment A: run A/B across 10% traffic for short-chat: INT8 vs FP16 using metric set: latency p50/p95/p99, eval_win_rate on 500 prompt set, error rate. Rolling period 2 weeks. JIRA: JIRA-OPT-412.
- Experiment B: embed-heavy batch job throughput test with 4-bit quant + 128 batch vs INT8 + 256 batch; measure tail latency and GPU utilization.
- Experiment C: FP8 variant with alternate kernel scheduling to observe stability in long-chat streaming scenarios (look for token-halting and calibration drift).

Actionable todo (next week):
- Liam: produce microbench harness outputs for open-arch-7B and a 13B variant with the three quant modes. Deadline: 2025-11-24.
- Sofia: assemble eval sets for short-chat (500 prompts) + summarization (200 docs) + offline human-sample labels. Deadline: 2025-11-20.
- Asha (owner): implement mapping script that converts kernel tokens/sec + hourly cost -> cost/1M tokens, store canonical table in /optimize/quant-profiles/ (PR prep).

Unresolved questions / risk flags:
- FP8 stability: some models show non-linear quality noise across seeds; need to confirm with at least 3 seeds.
- 4-bit safety: hallucination risk increases on chain-of-thought tasks; add additional guarded filters if enabling for production.
- Cost alignment: our platform overhead multiplier is heuristic; we should derive this from telemetry + cost-of-net/gateway on a per-namespace basis.

Appendix (calculation snapshots):
- Tokens/sec conversion: tokens_sec = kernel_tokens_sec * kernel_efficiency_factor(batching, kv_cache)
- Example: short-chat FP16 kernel_tokens_sec=12k, with 40% kv reuse adjusted_eff = 12k * (1 + 0.4*0.2) approx = 12k * 1.08 ~ 12.96k (we conservatively round to 12k in table).
- Cost per 1M = (1_000_000 / tokens_sec) seconds -> /3600 -> hours -> * hourly_cost -> + platform_overhead

Notes to self: keep this doc intentionally lightweight — it will evolve into a canonical spreadsheet with per-model tabs. Prefer to keep the recommendation rules simple and auditable so SRE/product can adopt quickly.
